title: Couples Holding Hands
description: Find the minimum swaps to seat every couple adjacently, using a greedy pair-by-pair fix-up with an O(1) position map.

blocks.text: n couples sit in 2n seats in a row, numbered 0 to 2n-1. Person 2i and person 2i+1 form couple i. A swap exchanges the positions of any two people. Return the minimum number of swaps so that every couple sits in adjacent seats.

blocks.caption: A position map lets each required swap locate the true partner in O(1), avoiding a rescan.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Field","Details"],"rows":[["Input","row[] (a permutation of 0 to 2n-1, person IDs)"],["Couple rule","Person 2i and person 2i+1 are couple i"],["Goal","Minimum swaps so every adjacent pair (seats 2k, 2k+1) is a couple"]]}

blocks.text: Processing seat pairs left to right and greedily fixing each pair (swapping in the correct partner if missing) is a classic greedy simulation. A position-tracking array (mapping each person to their current seat) turns "find where the partner currently sits" from an O(n) scan into an O(1) lookup, making each fix-up swap fast.

blocks.title: Connection
blocks.text: This is conceptually similar to cycle-detection swap-sorting problems: fixing one pair at a time, in order, and never needing to revisit an already-fixed pair, since each swap only ever affects positions at or after the current pair.

Picture a row of paired benches. Walking bench by bench, check if the two people currently seated there are already a couple. If not, fetch the true partner of the first person (wherever they currently sit) and swap them into the second seat of this bench, counting one swap. Since the first seat of each bench is never touched again, this greedy fix-up never needs to be revisited.

blocks.caption: Fixing one bench at a time, fetching the true partner when needed, never needs to revisit a completed bench.

items: Maintain posOf[person] = current seat index, for O(1) partner lookup.
For each seat pair (i, i+1), compute the true partner of the person at seat i.
If the person at seat i+1 is not that partner, swap the partner (from wherever they sit) into seat i+1, updating posOf for both swapped people, and count one swap.

blocks.title: Answer
blocks.text: Only 1 swap is needed, matching the expected output. After the single swap, every adjacent pair (0,1) and (2,3) is a valid couple.
A direct approach uses the same greedy fix-up-pair-by-pair strategy, but locates the true partner by scanning the array each time, which is correct but can cost O(n) per swap.

Maintaining a position map (updated as swaps happen) turns each partner lookup into O(1), since the map always reflects the array's current state. This keeps the overall algorithm at O(n) instead of O(n^2).
For each seat pair, if the partner is missing, scan forward to find them, swap them into place, and count the swap.

codes.python:
def min_swaps_couples(row):
    n = len(row)
    arr = row[:]
    swaps = 0

    for i in range(0, n, 2):
        partner = arr[i] + 1 if arr[i] % 2 == 0 else arr[i] - 1
        if arr[i + 1] != partner:
            j = arr.index(partner, i + 1)
            arr[i + 1], arr[j] = arr[j], arr[i + 1]
            swaps += 1

    return swaps


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(min_swaps_couples([0, 2, 1, 3]))
    print(min_swaps_couples([3, 2, 0, 1]))

blocks.title: Bottleneck
blocks.text: Scanning forward to find the partner every time is unnecessary once their exact position is tracked directly.

Maintain a position array mapping each person to their current seat index. For each seat pair, compute the true partner needed; if missing, look up the partner's seat in O(1), swap them into place, and update the position map for both people involved in the swap.

items: Build the position map once, O(n).
For each seat pair, an O(1) partner lookup and, if needed, an O(1) swap plus position map update.
Total time is O(n) across all seat pairs.

codes.python:
def min_swaps_couples(row):
    n = len(row)
    arr = row[:]
    pos_of = [0] * n
    for i, v in enumerate(arr):
        pos_of[v] = i

    swaps = 0
    for i in range(0, n, 2):
        partner = arr[i] + 1 if arr[i] % 2 == 0 else arr[i] - 1
        if arr[i + 1] != partner:
            j = pos_of[partner]
            pos_of[arr[i + 1]] = j
            pos_of[arr[j]] = i + 1
            arr[i + 1], arr[j] = arr[j], arr[i + 1]
            swaps += 1

    return swaps


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(min_swaps_couples([0, 2, 1, 3]))
    print(min_swaps_couples([3, 2, 0, 1]))

items: A greedy "fix one pair, never revisit it" strategy works whenever fixing the current position never disturbs already-fixed earlier positions.
A position map turns "find where this specific value currently is" from an O(n) scan into an O(1) lookup, a broadly reusable trick whenever elements are repeatedly swapped.
Keeping the position map updated after every swap (not just built once) is essential, since the array keeps changing.

blocks.text: Couples Holding Hands is solved with a greedy pair-by-pair fix-up: for each seat pair, if the true partner is missing, swap them in from their current position, tracked via a position map for O(1) lookup. Since each swap only affects positions at or after the current pair, no fixed pair is ever revisited, giving an O(n) solution.
